hints: Notice that W and X are the exact reverse of each other, and so are Y and Z, so picture their enthalpy level diagrams.
For any reversible pair, the endothermic direction must climb uphill further to reach the same transition state, so its activation energy is larger by the size of $\Delta H$.
Apply that rule to both pairs: compare the $-56$ versus $+56$ pair, then the $+11$ versus $-11$ pair, to see which Ea is bigger each time.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reverse pairs**

Think of this like going up and down the same hill. W and X go opposite ways between the same reactants and products, and Y and Z do the same.

$$\text{W} \rightleftharpoons \text{X} \quad \text{with} \quad \Delta H = -56 \text{ and } +56 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Z} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y} \quad \text{with} \quad \Delta H = -11 \text{ and } +11 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Link enthalpy change to activation energy**

Activation energy is the climb from your starting level to the top of the hill (the transition state). The top is the same both ways, so starting lower means a bigger climb.

Chemical rule:
$$\Delta H = E_a(\text{forward}) - E_a(\text{reverse})$$

**Apply to W versus X**

W is exothermic ($\Delta H = -56$), so products are lower than reactants. X starts from that low level and must climb extra high, so $E_a(\text{X}) = E_a(\text{W}) + 56$.

Conclusion: X is greater than W.

**Apply to Y versus Z**

Y is endothermic ($\Delta H = +11$), so it starts low and climbs up. Z is exothermic ($\Delta H = -11$) and starts high and goes down, so $E_a(\text{Y}) = E_a(\text{Z}) + 11$.

Conclusion: Y is greater than Z, giving X greater than W and Y greater than Z.

options.A: First half is right because X is the endothermic reverse of W, so X has the larger Ea. Second half is wrong because Z is exothermic ($-11$) and Y is endothermic ($+11$), so Z cannot be greater than Y.
options.B: Correct. The endothermic direction always has the larger activation energy for the same transition state. X (+56) is greater than W (-56), and Y (+11) is greater than Z (-11).
options.C: Both halves are reversed. This would mean the exothermic direction has the larger Ea, which is impossible if the transition state is common to forward and reverse. Students choose this if they think a more exothermic, faster reaction needs more energy to start.
options.D: Second half is right (Y greater than Z), but first half is wrong. W is exothermic and X is endothermic, so W cannot have the larger Ea. This comes from mixing up which reaction is uphill.
